title: The hospital with a tunnel for the dead

slides.text: THIS HOSPITAL HAD A TUNNEL FOR THE DEAD
Louisville, Kentucky. Waverly Hills Sanatorium. It opened in 1910 for patients with tuberculosis.
TB was killing thousands. The massive building you see now opened in 1926.
Before antibiotics, the cure was fresh air. Patients were wheeled onto open porches... even in winter.
Many never went home. Legends claim tens of thousands died here. Historians say it was far fewer, but still thousands.
To hide the deaths from other patients, bodies were sent down a 500-foot tunnel to the bottom of the hill. The 'body chute.'
New drugs beat TB, and the sanatorium closed in 1961. It became a nursing home, then closed for good in 1982.
For years it sat empty. Broken windows. Peeling paint. Long, dark halls.
Today it's one of America's most famous 'haunted' buildings. Night tours report shadow figures and voices in the halls.
